links.comparator_used: Gemma 2 base (off-the-shelf) model run in the same workflow
links.outcome: Accuracy of risk of bias judgments against the two-reviewer reference standard
links.effect: Raw TRoB-1 accuracy 73.3% (n=118) to 73.9% (n=119) vs 52.2% (n=84) to 60.2% (n=97) for the Gemma 2 base model; accuracy remained higher for TRoB-1 after excluding invalid base-model outputs
links.quote: In independent clinician-assisted assessments using the same workflow, raw TRoB-1 accuracy ranged from 73.3% (n=118) to 73.9% (n=119), compared with 52.2% (n=84) to 60.2% (n=97) for the Gemma 2 base model.

links.comparator_used: Raw TRoB-1 outputs without clinician verification
links.outcome: Accuracy, macro-F1 and high-risk-of-bias F1 of risk of bias judgments against the reference standard
links.effect: Accuracy rose from about 73% raw to 82.0% (n=132) to 84.5% (n=136) after verification; macro-F1 0.709 to 0.776; high-RoB F1 rose from 0.600 to 0.784 (clinician 1) and 0.571 to 0.821 (clinician 2); clinicians corrected 13 and 18 initially incorrect judgments; no correct judgment was changed to incorrect
links.quote: Clinician 1 corrected 13 initially incorrect judgments and clinician 2 corrected 18.
